input.vignette:
A 65-year-old man presents with four months of low-grade fever and malaise. He also says he has lost 9 kg (20 lb) during this period and suffers from extreme fatigue. Past medical history is significant for a mitral valve replacement five years ago. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), respirations are 22/min, pulse is 102/min, and blood pressure is 138/78 mm Hg. On physical examination, there is a new onset 2/6 holosystolic murmur, loudest in the apical area of the precordium. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of this patient’s condition?

Options:
A. *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*
B. *Bartonella henselae*
C. HACEK group organisms
D. *Candida albicans*
E. Beta-hemolytic streptococci
F. *Staphylococcus aureus*
G. Coagulase-negative *Staphylococcus spp.*
H. *Pseudomonas* aeruginosa
I. *Streptococcus bovis*
J. *Enterococcus*

knowledge_chunks.title: Role of Cardiac CT in the Evaluation of Valvular Heart Disease. > PROSTHETIC-VALVE DISEASE
knowledge_chunks.text: Prosthetic-valve dysfunction is a complex clinical entity in which accurate differentiation of the underlying mechanisms is essential for appropriate management. In mechanical prosthetic valves, stenosis commonly results from thrombus formation, pannus ingrowth, or a combination of both. In contrast, bioprosthetic-valve stenosis is typically caused by structural valve degeneration, including leaflet thickening, calcification, and tearing, but may also be associated with thrombosis, IE, or pannus formation. Cine cardiac CT enables dynamic assessment of prosthetic-valve leaflet motion, allowing measurement of the opening and closing angles of mechanical valves and detection of abnormal tissue on or adjacent to the valve. The existing guidelines recommend cardiac CT as a key imaging modality for treatment planning when prosthetic-valve stenosis is suspected, particularly when echocardiographic findings are inconclusive. In addition, paravalvular leakage (PVL) may occur as a result of suture-line disruption related to technical factors, annular dehiscence, or IE, further contributing to prosthetic-valve dysfunction.
